elements.element: Services are performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly warrants that Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner by qualified personnel.

elements.element: The Services performance warranty remains effective for 90 days.
elements.evidence: No 90-day duration is stated for Services. Section 19.2 applies only to Deliverables and software; not all Services are necessarily Deliverables. An unstated duration does not satisfy the express duration requirement.

elements.element: Service Deliverables materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 warrants that Deliverables materially conform to their documentation and agreed specifications.

elements.element: The conformity warranty for Service Deliverables remains effective for 90 days after delivery or first availability.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 expressly provides a 90-day conformity warranty for each Deliverable.

elements.element: Software materially conforms to its documentation.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 expressly provides that any software will materially conform to its documentation.

elements.element: The software conformity warranty remains effective for 12 months.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 provides only 90 days for software, not 12 months.

elements.element: Vendor promptly re-performs or repairs a nonconforming item at no charge.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires Vendor to promptly re-perform or repair the nonconforming item at no charge.

elements.element: Vendor promptly replaces a nonconforming item at no charge.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 expressly includes prompt replacement at no charge.

elements.element: If Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of the Fees paid for it.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides this termination and refund remedy if Vendor cannot re-perform, repair, or replace within a reasonable period.
The rendered clause contains no warranty or covenant requiring compliance with applicable laws.

elements.element: Deliverables and software contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no malicious-code warranty.

elements.element: Services are performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: Section 19.1 expressly provides this Services performance warranty.

elements.element: The Services performance warranty remains effective for 30 days.
elements.evidence: The clause does not state a 30-day duration for Services. The 90-day language in Section 19.2 covers Deliverables and software only, so the non-operative margin comment cannot supply the missing Services duration.

elements.element: Software materially conforms to its documentation.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 expressly warrants software conformity to documentation.

elements.element: The software conformity warranty remains effective for 90 days after delivery or first availability.
elements.evidence: Section 19.2 expressly provides a 90-day period for software.

elements.element: Vendor promptly re-performs or repairs a nonconforming item at no charge.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 requires prompt re-performance or repair at no charge.

elements.element: Vendor promptly replaces a nonconforming item at no charge.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 expressly includes prompt replacement at no charge.

elements.element: If Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period, Customer may terminate the affected item and receive a refund of the Fees paid for it.
elements.evidence: Section 19.4 provides termination and refund if Vendor cannot cure within a reasonable period.

result.reason: The operative redline does not meet the fallback despite the margin comment: it gives software and Deliverables 90 days but never states a 30-day duration for the Services performance warranty. It also misses the preferred 12-month software period, express 90-day Services duration, compliance-with-laws warranty, and malicious-code warranty. The revisions otherwise preserve the existing remedy structure and unrelated terms, but the overlap between Section 19.1's undated Deliverables warranty and Section 19.2's 90-day warranty also creates avoidable duration ambiguity.
